title: Pricing by hours per project for Deck and fence maintenance
audience: Deck and fence maintenance owners who price multi-day jobs from estimated hours, and who need a cost per productive hour that covers materials and seasonal gaps.
learningOutcomes: Calculate a cost per productive hour from the owner's own figures, including vehicle and tool costs
Estimate a deck or fence job by component, including travel, set-up and checking time
Build a quote from hours, materials and a margin, and state its basis and exclusions

instruction.heading: Why deck work starts from hours
instruction.body: A deck job mixes labour that depends on the condition of the boards and the access, with materials bought by area or length. Hours make the labour visible. The vendor listing for Victoria gives board renewal per linear metre, joists and bearers per linear metre, and posts per post. It does not separate the labour inside those prices, so the owner needs hours from their own log.

instruction.heading: Work out the cost per productive hour
instruction.body: Divide the year's running costs by chargeable hours. Running costs include crew wages with on-costs where you employ anyone, the vehicle and trailer, power tools, sanding and cutting blades, ladder or scaffold hire if you pay for it, insurance, state licence fees, phone, software and administration. Business.gov.au says on-costs such as leave and superannuation belong in the hourly cost. Pay rates for employees may be set by an award or enterprise agreement, and this lesson does not state them.

instruction.heading: Estimate the job by component
instruction.body: Break the job into components: strip and assess, board removal, board fitting, joist and bearer checks, post and footing checks, sanding or cleaning, finishing coats, clean-up and disposal, and travel. Estimate each as a range. Add a buffer for unexpected work: Xero's Australian guide suggests 10 to 20 per cent. Carters Trade Leader, a New Zealand source, recommends comparing each quote with the actual labour to correct the next estimate.

instruction.heading: Price the materials and the margin
instruction.body: The vendor listing gives board supply by area: treated pine at $25 to $50 per square metre, and spotted gum at $110 to $200 per square metre (The Quote Yard, 2 May 2026). Apply your materials policy. Business Queensland's example adds additional costs at cost plus 15 per cent. That is a suggestion from one source, not a benchmark. Then set the price with a margin: the price is the total cost divided by one minus the margin.

instruction.heading: Keep the quote honest and review it
instruction.body: State the scope by component, what is excluded, such as rot found under the deck, permit fees and approvals, and reconnection of fixed items, what the client must provide, such as access and clear space, and how long the quote is valid. Re-quote on any change. Record actual hours for each component for at least the first ten jobs and compare them with the estimate.

procedure: Gather the year's total business costs and the chargeable hours from the same period.
Divide total costs by chargeable hours to get the cost per productive hour, and date the figure.
Break the job into components and estimate each as a range.
Add travel, set-up, clean-up and checking time as named lines.
Add a buffer for unexpected work, then multiply the labour hours by the cost per productive hour.
Add materials at your policy, then apply the margin and the minimum charge.
Write the quote with scope by component, hours basis, exclusions, client inputs and validity.
Record actual hours for each component after the job and compare them with the estimate.

workedExamples.situation: Illustrative figures only, not market rates. A 20 square metre timber deck needs its boards renewed. The estimate is 14 crew-hours on site. The owner's cost per productive hour is $70 (illustrative). The buffer is 10 per cent on labour (illustrative). Treated pine boards are used at the low end of the vendor range, $25 per square metre, which is $500 in total. The target margin on price is 25 per cent (illustrative).
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the cost, what is the price, and what happens if the boards are priced at the top of the vendor range?
workedExamples.reasoning: Labour is 14 hours multiplied by $70, which is $980. A 10 per cent buffer on labour adds $98, for $1,078 of labour. Materials at $500 bring the total cost to $1,578 (illustrative). A 25 per cent margin on price gives a price of $1,578 divided by 0.75, which is $2,104 (illustrative). The vendor range for full board renewal of a 20 square metre deck is $1,800 to $5,500 per job (The Quote Yard, 2 May 2026), so the illustrative price sits at the low end of that range. At the top of the vendor board-supply range, $50 per square metre, materials would be $1,000 and the total cost $2,078, which gives a price of $2,770.67 (illustrative). If the inspection finds rot in joists, the joist work is a separate priced variation, using the vendor joist range of $40 to $80 per linear metre as a check, and it is approved in writing before it is done.

equipmentAndPpe: Quote worksheet or spreadsheet, with a line for each component
Time log for each job, with estimated and actual columns
Measuring tape or laser measure for deck area and board length
PPE as set by {{business:safety.required_ppe}}, and the safety data sheet for any finish or stain used

commonErrors.error: Pricing from the hourly wage alone
commonErrors.prevention: Include on-costs, vehicle, tools, consumables, insurance and administration in the cost per productive hour.

commonErrors.error: Counting paid hours as productive hours
commonErrors.prevention: Use chargeable hours only when calculating the cost per productive hour.

commonErrors.error: Leaving out materials policy or the buffer for unexpected work
commonErrors.prevention: Add materials and a stated buffer to every estimate, and state them on the quote.

commonErrors.error: Quoting with no exclusions for rot, permits or reconnection
commonErrors.prevention: List each exclusion, and price any variation before the work starts.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Pricing guidance only. The ACCC says misleading statements about prices are prohibited, and state fair trading rules differ. Check the rules for your state.
Pay rates, allowances and on-costs for employees may be set by an award or enterprise agreement. This lesson does not state those rates.

Queensland: building work above $3,300 including materials, labour and GST needs a licence. New South Wales: minor maintenance above $5,000 in labour and materials including GST needs a licence, and the research did not check whether deck or fence work is minor maintenance under the schedule. Check both before you quote a deck job.
Council permits can change the scope. A deck may need a building permit, so include permit fees and approvals as an exclusion or as a priced line.

qualityStandard: Each quote shows scope by component, hours or price basis, exclusions, client inputs and validity.
The cost per productive hour is calculated from the owner's own records and dated.
Actual hours are recorded for each component for at least the first ten jobs and compared with the estimate.
documentationEvidence: Cost per productive hour worksheet, dated, with the source of each figure
Quote showing scope by component, hours basis, exclusions and validity
Job time log with estimated and actual hours by component
summary: Start every deck quote from hours, broken down by component.
Cost per productive hour uses chargeable time, not paid time.
Materials, buffer, permits and rot are named lines, not hidden extras.
Compare estimates with actual hours by component, and change the method when they diverge.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which costs belong in the cost per productive hour for a deck business?
options: Only the wage of the lowest-paid worker
The price the client pays, plus any deposit taken
Wages with on-costs, vehicle, tools, consumables, insurance and administration, divided by chargeable hours
The average price that competitors advertise for decking

knowledgeChecks.question: A deck job estimated at 14 crew-hours takes 20. What is the right response?
options: Record the actual hours by component, find the cause, and change the estimate and future quotes
Leave the estimate alone, since the client has paid
Cut paid hours for the crew on the next job
Raise the price for this client's next job only

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should rot found under the boards be an exclusion or a priced variation?
options: Because the customer should pay for it without seeing a price
Because the condition is unknown until the boards are lifted, so the change must be priced and approved
Because rot is never part of a deck job
Because it lowers the margin on every other line

sourceReferences: business.gov.au, 'Choose a pricing strategy', https://business.gov.au/products-and-services/choose-a-pricing-strategy, page metadata dated 1 October 2026. On-costs such as leave and superannuation belong in the hourly cost.
ACCC, 'Setting prices: what's allowed', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/pricing/setting-prices-whats-allowed, last modified 15 July 2026. Misleading price statements are prohibited.
Xero Australia, 'How to price services', https://www.xero.com/au/guides/how-to-price-services/, dated 3 September 2026. Divide by billable hours; 10 to 20 per cent allowance for unexpected work.

Carters Trade Leader, 'Estimating how many hours a job will take', https://tradeleader.carters.co.nz/trade-skills/estimating-how-many-hours-a-job-will-take-why-83-get-it-wrong/, dated 1 October 2025. New Zealand source; compare quoted with actual labour.

The Quote Yard, Timber deck repair and restoration Victoria, https://www.thequoteyard.com.au/services/timber-deck-repair-and-restoration-carpentry-vic, published 2 May 2026. Vendor estimates for board supply and board renewal, used only as checks.

Business Queensland, 'Preparing a business quote: tips', https://www.business.qld.gov.au/running-business/marketing-sales/sales/preparing-quote/tips, last updated 16 November 2022. Additional costs at cost plus 15 per cent is one source's suggestion.

Boroondara City Council, 'Deck permits', https://www.boroondara.vic.gov.au/planning-building/do-i-need-permit/deck-permits, last modified 11 August 2026. A building permit is always needed to build a deck.

Queensland Building and Construction Commission, 'Licence required for building work', https://www.qbcc.qld.gov.au/node/7081, last reviewed 16 April 2026. Licence above $3,300 including materials, labour and GST.

NSW Government, 'Minor maintenance and cleaning work', https://www.nsw.gov.au/business-and-economy/licences-and-credentials/building-and-trade-licences-and-registrations/minor-maintenance-and-cleaning-work, last updated 23 June 2026. Licence above $5,000 in labour and materials including GST.
